name: Register ability and expose to REST
query: I want to add a new ability for my plugin feature and have the client UI check it via REST. What should I change?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Run wordpress-router to classify repo kind
Step 2: Run wp-project-triage to detect plugin structure
Step 4: Register ability category if needed with wp_register_ability_category()
Step 6: Set meta.public to true for exposure on WP 7.1+ (meta.show_in_rest to true on 6.9/7.0), reaching for show_in_rest on 7.1+ only as a per-channel override
Step 7: Decide MCP exposure in the same edit and set meta.mcp.public explicitly — on MCP Adapter 0.6.0+ an unqualified meta.public is inherited as MCP exposure
Step 9: Verify endpoint returns the new ability

Step 11: Name the ability as namespace/name matching Core's /^[a-z0-9-]+\/[a-z0-9-]+$/ — my-plugin/get-info is valid, my_plugin/get-info is not, because underscores are rejected and the registration silently returns null

Step 12: State that property-level input_schema defaults are not injected by PHP but ARE mutated into the input by the client's AJV (useDefaults: true), so the callback must normalize defaults itself rather than relying on either transport
Step 13: Use the full run route /wp-abilities/v1/abilities/{name}/run when showing execution over REST
Step 14: Treat an awaited @wordpress/core-abilities ready as settled, not succeeded — an empty store after awaiting it can still mean an authentication or network failure
success_criteria: Enables REST exposure with the version-correct meta key (meta.public on 7.1+, meta.show_in_rest on 6.9/7.0)
Declares meta.mcp.public explicitly rather than letting MCP exposure be inherited from meta.public
Documents REST endpoint wp-abilities/v1 and uses the full run path /wp-abilities/v1/abilities/{name}/run
Uses a hyphenated namespace/name that satisfies Core's name regex and does not use an underscore
Does not claim schema defaults reach the callback on both transports; separates PHP behaviour from the client's AJV useDefaults behaviour
Does not treat a resolved core-abilities ready promise as proof the fetch succeeded
